_about: What Dana is earning for. Rungs are bought in any order their requirements allow; the million is a milestone, not a purchase. Costs climb steeply so the top is a long way off.

rungs.name: Adopt Pickle
rungs.blurb: A scruffy terrier from the shelter on Mill Lane. He rides in the cab and sleeps under the desk.
rungs.effect: Pickle greets every customer: tips +5%. Food is $4 a day.

mail.subject: Pickle is yours
mail.body:
Dana,

The paperwork's done. He answers to Pickle, mostly. He likes the front seat and does not like the hoover.

Send us a photo when he's settled.

— Jo, Mill Lane Shelter

rungs.name: A room of her own
rungs.blurb: Dana has been sleeping on the garage sofa since Grayline let her go. A rented room over the laundromat, with a window.
rungs.effect: Rested: the first job each day pays a 10% bigger tip.

mail.subject: Heard you got a bed
mail.body:
About time. The sofa was a tax write-off, not a plan.

Sleep. The truck will still be there.

— Mile Marker

rungs.name: Hire Ray
rungs.blurb: Ray Dunbar, ex-Grayline, carries a sofa like it's a loaf. He wants a wage and a radio he can choose.
rungs.effect: One more job on the board every day.

mail.subject: Start Monday
mail.body:
Boss,

I'll be at the garage at seven. I bring my own gloves. I do not bring my own radio, so we'll need to talk about that.

Ray

rungs.name: A second truck
rungs.blurb: A used box van with a dent Ray says gives it character. Ray takes it out on his own run every day.
rungs.effect: Ray's run brings in a job's pay every night, without you.

mail.subject: The van
mail.body:
She pulls to the left and the radio only gets one station. I love her.

First run tomorrow. I'll leave the money in the tin.

Ray

rungs.name: The flat on Quay Street
rungs.blurb: Two rooms, a balcony the width of a chair, and a view of the river if you lean. Dana's name on the buzzer.
rungs.effect: A proper kitchen: Dana cooks for the crew. Customers feel it: vibe +4.

mail.subject: Housewarming?
mail.body:
Hi Dana,

It's Sam, from the Thursday delivery. You mentioned the flat. If you're having people round I make a good lasagne and I'm told I'm good at carrying things, which seems relevant.

No pressure.

Sam

rungs.name: A second counter
rungs.blurb: The empty unit by the station, fitted out like the yard: a counter, a grinder, and someone you trust on the till.
rungs.effect: A second shop earns half of what the yard takes, every night.

mail.subject: Two shops
mail.body:
Two shops. My first partner said never open a second one until the first one bores you.

Is it boring you yet?

— Mile Marker

rungs.name: A third truck, and Mei
rungs.blurb: Mei Tanaka drove coaches for twenty years and reverses better than you. A newer van, this time with two working stations.
rungs.effect: Mei's run joins Ray's: two jobs' pay a night.

mail.subject: Keys
mail.body:
Dana,

The keys are on the hook. I checked the tyres; two were low. They aren't now.

I'll take the long routes. Nobody tips for a dent.

Mei

rungs.name: A house of her own
rungs.blurb: A terrace on Elm Row with a garden Pickle can dig up. Sam moves in, with the lasagne dish.
rungs.effect: Sam packs the crew's lunches: every job's tips +10%.

mail.subject: Keys, plural
mail.body:
We have keys. Plural. I have put the lasagne dish in the cupboard by the cooker, which I believe makes this official.

Pickle has already found the one soft patch in the lawn.

Sam

rungs.name: A family
rungs.blurb: A cot in the back bedroom, a pram in the hall, and the first client Dana cannot say no to.
rungs.effect: Word gets round: Rep +2, and the day ends an hour earlier.

mail.subject: Congratulations
mail.body:
I've sent a bear. It is too big. That is the point of a bear.

Take the week. Ray can drive.

— Mile Marker

rungs.name: The depot
rungs.blurb: The old Grayline yard on Harbour Road, with the sign taken down. Room for six trucks and a kettle that never cools.
rungs.effect: Three more trucks and crews: five runs a night.

mail.subject: The yard
mail.body:
Boss. The Grayline yard. I had my locker there for nine years.

I've put my new locker in the same spot. Feels right.

Ray

rungs.name: Three counters
rungs.blurb: The third counter opens by the park. The name on the window is in the same hand on all three.
rungs.effect: Two more shops: each earns half of the yard's takings a night.

mail.subject: A conversation
mail.body:
Ms Reyes,

We note your business now spans three units, two of them ours. We would like to discuss terms over lunch, which we will pay for, which should tell you something.

— Hollis Property

rungs.name: Ten trucks
rungs.blurb: Ten vans in Corner Office cream, a dispatcher, and a weekly fuel bill with a comma in it.
rungs.effect: Five more runs a night. The town knows the trucks by name.

mail.subject: Ten
mail.body:
Ten vans. I have taught the new drivers to reverse. Four of them can.

We need a bigger kettle.

Mei

rungs.name: Corner Office, everywhere
rungs.blurb: Counters in four towns and a truck in each. Dana signs things now, mostly.
rungs.effect: Six more shops across the county, each earning a share of the yard's takings.

mail.subject: The sign
mail.body:
I drove past a Corner Office in Harbourmouth today. Same lettering. Same bad coffee, I assume.

I am very proud and I will deny saying so.

— Mile Marker

milestones.name: The first million
milestones.blurb: A million dollars earned, one box at a time.

mail.subject: A million
mail.body:
Dana,

A million. From a garage that smelled of diesel.

My first partner said the first million is the hard one. He was wrong about most things. We'll see about that.

— Mile Marker

milestones.name: Ten million
milestones.blurb: Ten million earned. Marge frames the first invoice.

mail.subject: Ten
mail.body:
Ten million. I framed your first invoice. It was for $100 and you spelled 'receipt' wrong.

— Mile Marker

milestones.name: A hundred million
milestones.blurb: Grayline, who let Dana go, offer to buy the lot.

mail.subject: An offer
mail.body:
Ms Reyes,

Grayline would like to acquire Corner Office in full for $250,000,000. The offer stands for as long as you like. We note you once worked for us. We note it with some embarrassment.

Grayline Logistics

milestones.name: The billion
milestones.blurb: A billion dollars earned, starting from a garage and a borrowed truck.

mail.subject: A note to myself
mail.body:
Day one: $120, a garage, and a truck I didn't own.

Today: a billion. Pickle is asleep under the desk. Sam says dinner's at seven.

I think I'll do a job tomorrow. A small one. By hand.

Dana

empire.name: A depot in Harbourmouth
empire.blurb: The second yard, forty miles down the coast, with Mei running it and a sign in the same lettering.
empire.effect: Ten more trucks on the road every night.

mail.subject: Harbourmouth
mail.body:
Dana,

The yard's open. The drivers are young and the vans are new, so I have put a dent in one myself, for luck.

Mei

empire.name: The Corner Office fund
empire.blurb: Marge's accountant, a woman called Dilys who does not blink, puts the jar to work.
empire.effect: The jar grows by 1% every night.

mail.subject: Your money, working
mail.body:
Ms Reyes,

I have placed the funds. You will see the number move at night. Do not watch it. People who watch it ring me.

D. Pryce

empire.name: The Harbour Road units
empire.blurb: Hollis Property sells you the row your first shops rent. The lunch was good.
empire.effect: Rent comes in instead of going out: $3,000 a night.

mail.subject: Keys, and a confession
mail.body:
Ms Reyes,

The deeds are yours. We confess we always liked the lettering.

— Hollis Property, tenants

empire.name: Fifty trucks
empire.blurb: A fleet with a fleet manager, a paint shop, and a Christmas party that needs a hall.

mail.subject: Fifty
mail.body:
Boss. Fifty vans. I counted them twice because I didn't believe it the first time.

I still drive the dented one.

Ray

empire.name: Dilys goes further
empire.blurb: A second fund, a lawyer, and a letter from the bank with your name spelled right.
empire.effect: The jar grows by 2% every night.

mail.subject: Further
mail.body:
Ms Reyes,

We are, as they say, in the market now. I have bought you a coat for the meetings. It is grey. Wear it.

D. Pryce

empire.name: Corner Office, county-wide
empire.blurb: Twenty counters in twenty towns, and a training kitchen where the yard used to be.
empire.effect: Twenty more counters earning every night.

mail.subject: The county
mail.body:
Twenty towns. I drove to four of them today for the coffee. It was consistent, which is a kind of compliment.

— Mile Marker

empire.name: The rail yard contract
empire.blurb: Every freight container off the night train, moved by morning, forever.

mail.subject: Contract 7719
mail.body:
Ms Reyes,

The first train is at 02:10. It will not wait. Neither will the second.

Freight Operations

empire.name: The bank charter
empire.blurb: Corner Office Savings. Dilys runs it. The coat is navy now.
empire.effect: The jar grows by 3% every night.

mail.subject: A bank
mail.body:
Ms Reyes,

We are a bank. I have never written that sentence before. Please stop keeping cash in a jar.

D. Pryce

empire.name: The Corner Office tower
empire.blurb: Thirty floors on Harbour Road with the garage preserved in the lobby, oil stain and all.
empire.effect: $150,000 a night from the tenants, and the whole town knows the name.

mail.subject: The lobby
mail.body:
They kept the garage. The actual garage. Pickle found the oil stain in about four seconds.

Come home. Lasagne.

Sam

empire.name: Every town on the map
empire.blurb: A Corner Office in every town that has a map. Dana still takes one job a week herself, in the dented van.
empire.effect: $500,000 a night, and the last stretch to the billion.

mail.subject: Every town
mail.body:
I am retired. I am very retired. I have a map on the wall with a pin for every one.

There are a lot of pins, Dana.

— Mile Marker

mail.subject: Completion
mail.body:
Ms Reyes,

The funds have cleared. The fleet, the counters, the tower and the name are Grayline's. We will keep the lettering.

You are welcome back any time, in any capacity.

Grayline Logistics

events.line: The tax office looked at the books and took 2% of the jar for the trouble.
Brightway Removals undercut three of the runs tonight.
The Harbourmouth drivers struck for a day. Mei settled it with a kettle.
A museum paid $25,000 to move one very old chair very slowly.
